title: A message broker that understands tokens
subtitle: Scheduling GPU inference by the shape of the work, so two different cards ran at a 99.9 percent cache hit rate with almost no padding

stats.label: padding waste across one shared backlog
lines of Rust in four crates

lede: A general-purpose queue moves bytes and knows nothing about what they cost to run. GPU inference cost depends almost entirely on the shape of the work: how long the prompts are, how much each prompt shares with its neighbours, how much padding a batch carries. I built a broker whose unit of scheduling is the token. It organises incoming work so that each batch is shape-pure, packs batches to each GPU's declared limits, and delivers them so the engine's cache keeps hitting. I had a backlog of billions of tokens to generate and two GPUs of different sizes to do it with. A conventional queue would hand each card whatever came next.
quote: Four integers describe any consumer, including ones that do not exist yet.
evidence: Token-aware scheduling: a Rust broker that batches GPU inference by prompt shape, with 0.421% padding waste across one shared backlog and 0 shape switches mid-stream.
Message broker and queue design: a four-crate Rust broker of about 24,000 lines with a disk-backed, shape-pure backlog that survives restarts.
Inference serving architecture: every consumer described by four numbers, so a 32 GB and a 16 GB NVIDIA Blackwell card drained one backlog at a 99.9 percent cache hit rate.
author: Corey James
